explanation: The Roman governor who succeeded Felix as ruler of Judea.
The apostle Paul, a Christian preacher who was accused of being a rebel and charged in Jerusalem.
One or more formal charges brought by Jewish leaders against Paul during his trial.
The former Roman governor of Judea, who had kept Paul imprisoned before Festus took office.
The Roman emperor in Rome; Paul appealed his case to him to avoid unfair treatment locally.
The Jewish religious and civil rules that the accusers claimed Paul had broken.
The term used for the political or social unrest in Judea, which the governor was concerned about.
The place where Paul was held imprisoned while his case was being handled by Roman authorities.
